prose: Short note from feed metadata only: the Washington Post tested chatbots on US midterm voter questions and found they lean heavily on three obscure, AI-built voter-information sites - Copilot cited the error-prone Ballot Brief in 75% of its test answers, ChatGPT in 22%. The sites, including one built by Ben Torres Ezrick as a one-stop shop for voters, are themselves AI-generated. The Post's page is paywalled, so the test methodology and error examples are unverified here, but the shape of the finding - chatbots laundering AI-generated civic content into authoritative answers - matches the tests described.
highlights: WaPo tests: chatbots answer midterm questions from three obscure AI-built voter sites
Copilot cited the error-prone Ballot Brief in 75% of tests; ChatGPT in 22%
The voter sites are themselves AI-generated - synthetic civic content feeding authoritative answers
Paywalled; methodology unverified, shape of the finding matches the feed description
